hypothesis: block 47 fails because the trunk Pairformer carries its SINGLE-track residual in bf16 while the residual has grown far past the size of the per-block update, so the update is quantised away. tt_bio/tenstorrent.py already implements the remedy as `s_fp32_residual`, and openfold3_confidence.py:101 already turns it on for the CONFIDENCE Pairformer. openfold3_trunk.py:152 does not pass it, so the trunk runs at the default False.
caveats: s_norm is an L2 norm over the probe tensor, not an absmax, so it cannot be compared directly to the 2.28e5 absmax cited in the s_fp32_residual comment without the tensor shape.

The per-block fractional update figures are SEGMENT MEANS over 23 and 24 blocks, not local values at blocks 23 and 47; the true profile declines monotonically and the local value at block 47 is smaller than the segment mean shown.

Block 23 already sits at 70.7 percent of block 47 s_norm yet its gradient median is 49x better. s_norm alone therefore does NOT order the failures, and the experiment must carry block 23 as a control. If block 23 does not move and block 47 does, the mechanism is threshold-like; if both move, it is graded; if neither moves, the hypothesis is refuted.
This is a forward-residual dtype change. Whether it reaches the WEIGHT gradient is exactly what the experiment measures and is not assumed here.
Turning it on in the trunk is release-gated: it changes accuracy and costs one [B, L, c_s] fp32 tensor. Keep it on the branch, flag it, do not merge it.
experiment: re-run the existing crop-64 instrument-A arms at blocks 0, 23 and 47 with the trunk Pairformer constructed s_fp32_residual=True, everything else identical. One flag, three arms, same harness, same frozen bundle.
prediction_registered_before_the_run: block 47 median falls by more than 2x; block 0 moves by less than 20 percent; the pair track (tri_mul_*, tri_att_*) moves less than the single track (attn_pair_bias.*, single_transition.*), because z does not grow through the stack (0.980x) while s does (367x).
